summary:
Nikolaus von Schönberg was a German Catholic cardinal and Archbishop of Capua. He played a crucial role in the Catholic Church's reorganization during the late Middle Ages. The appointment of new cardinals, such as Johannes von Hohenzollern, marked a significant turning point for the Church. This period also saw increased tensions between the papacy and secular European powers. The appointment of cardinals was often influenced by regional politics and power struggles. Ultimately, Nikolaus von Schönberg's legacy lies in his contributions to the Catholic Church's governance structure.

Nikolaus von Schönberg's tenure as Archbishop of Capua spanned several decades, during which he oversaw the implementation of various reforms aimed at strengthening the Church's authority. These efforts were often at odds with the growing power of secular monarchies and city-states. The appointment of cardinals was a key aspect of this process, allowing the papacy to exert influence over regional politics.

The legacy of Nikolaus von Schönberg can be seen in the modern structure of the Catholic Church's governance. His reforms paved the way for the development of more centralized power within the Church, which has had far-reaching consequences for its relations with secular powers and the broader world.

The influence of Nikolaus von Schönberg on regional politics is still felt today, as many European countries continue to grapple with the legacy of the Catholic Church's role in shaping their histories. His appointment of cardinals helped to cement the Church's position as a major player in European affairs during this period.
